subproblem.title: Mean deviation is bounded by the double-integral oscillation on a set of volume 1
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, let S ⊆ Euclid (m + 1) be any set with Lebesgue measure vol(S) = 1, and let u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ be integrable on S. Then, with c := ∫_S u, ∫_{x∈S}|u(x) − c| dx ≤ ∫_{x∈S}∫_{y∈S}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), volume S = 1 → IntegrableOn u S → ∫ x in S, |u x - ∫ y in S, u y| ≤ ∫ x in S, ∫ y in S, |u x - u y|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (c := ∫_{Q₁}u; since vol(Q₁) = 1, u(x) − c = ∫_{Q₁}(u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − c| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy = h_0(x); integrate over Q₁), stated for an arbitrary set S of volume 1. The integrability of the inner integral h is step 1 of the parent proof.

Notation. Euclid (m + 1) with Lebesgue measure vol. μ := vol restricted to S (Measure.restrict is defined for every set S). Integrals ∫ … dμ are exactly the set integrals ∫_S … of the statement. c := ∫ u dμ = ∫_S u.

1. μ is a probability measure: μ(univ) = vol(S) = 1 (Measure.restrict_apply_univ, valid for every set S). In particular μ is finite, constants are μ-integrable, and ∫ b dμ = μ(univ)·b = b for every constant b (integral_const). By hypothesis u ∈ L¹(μ).
2. Integrability on the product. On μ ⊗ μ the functions (x, y) ↦ u(x) and (x, y) ↦ u(y) are integrable (Integrable.comp_fst and Integrable.comp_snd, using that μ is finite). Hence F(x, y) := |u(x) − u(y)| is μ⊗μ-integrable (difference, then absolute value), and by Fubini (Integrable.integral_prod_left) h(x) := ∫ |u(x) − u(y)| dμ(y) is a μ-integrable function of x.
3. Pointwise bound. Fix x. The function y ↦ u(x) − u(y) is μ-integrable (a constant minus u), and by linearity (integral_sub) and step 1, ∫ (u(x) − u(y)) dμ(y) = u(x) − ∫ u dμ = u(x) − c. Hence |u(x) − c| = |∫ (u(x) − u(y)) dμ(y)| ≤ ∫ |u(x) − u(y)| dμ(y) = h(x), because the absolute value of an integral is at most the integral of the absolute value (abs_integral_le_integral_abs).
4. Integration. The function x ↦ |u(x) − c| is nonnegative and pointwise ≤ h(x), and h is μ-integrable by step 2. By monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono_of_nonneg: nonnegative left side, integrable right side, pointwise inequality), ∫ |u(x) − c| dμ(x) ≤ ∫ h dμ = ∫_{x∈S}∫_{y∈S}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx. With c = ∫_S u this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ := vol restricted to S has μ(univ) = vol(S) = 1, so it is a probability measure and u ∈ L¹(μ).
Fubini: |u(x) − u(y)| is μ⊗μ-integrable, so h(x) := ∫_S|u(x) − u(y)| dy is integrable on S.
Since μ(univ) = 1, u(x) − ∫_S u = ∫_S (u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − ∫_S u| ≤ h(x).
Integrating the nonnegative function |u − ∫_S u| ≤ h over S gives ∫_S|u − ∫_S u| ≤ ∫_S∫_S|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.

audit.reason: The exact proposition correctly permits arbitrary S: restrict_apply_univ requires no measurability assumption on S. Unit mass justifies the constant-integral identity, product integrability justifies Fubini, and the absolute-integral inequality followed by integration proves the conclusion completely without circular reliance.
